newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor climbs after oil shale news.
newsitem.headline: Suncor climbs after oil shale news.

text.p: Shares in Suncor Energy Inc jumped on Wednesday after the Calgary-based company and its Australian partners said their proposed oil shale project in Queensland moved a step closer to fruition.

Suncor said construction of phase one of the Stuart oil shale project -- a pilot operation that would produce about 4,500 barrels of oil a day -- would start once Southern Pacific Petroleum NL and Central Pacific Minerals NL finalized their financing for the project.
Suncor climbed 1.35 to 35.60 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on volume of more than 134,000 shares.
"We now have one last hurdle to get over that's really with regards to SPP and CPM raising some money," Suncor chief financial officer David Byler said in a telephone interview.
The Australian partners were expected to finalize their funding for the project within the next 30 to 60 days, Byler said.
Initial production from the project could then start sometime in 1999, with Suncor contributing up to C$242 million (A$222 million).

If phase one proved the commercial viability of the technology -- which includes use of the Alberta-developed Taciuk Processor to extract oil from the shale -- output from the operation could grow to 85,000 barrels a day within 10 years, Suncor said.
"Phase one is really a demonstration of the technology and ability to prove up that we can scale this technology up to a commercial level," Byler said.
"There's a pilot plant here in Calgary that produces about 80 barrels a day. But this is a significant scale up from 80 to 4,500 barrels a day."
He said Suncor continued to look for other potential projects around the world where it could export the technology it uses at its big oil sands operation in northern Alberta.
None was at an announcement stage, he said.
